findings.title: Audit logs wired to a numeric paginator for a datetime column
findings.body: When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That class's get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. DateTimePaginator was the previous implementation because a datetime cannot be floored and the SQL bound must be a timezone-aware datetime, not an int. This path therefore raises TypeError while building the next cursor, or compares the datetime column to an integer, so any org owner or superuser who passes the query flag gets a 500 (or a wrong page) instead of audit logs.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features is not a paginate() argument
findings.body: The new branch calls self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True). Endpoint.paginate does not accept that keyword and does not forward arbitrary kwargs into the paginator constructor. The call either raises TypeError immediately or silently drops the flag, so OptimizedCursorPaginator.enable_advanced_features stays false and the branch that was supposed to change pagination never runs. The feature is also gated only by request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access, which is ordinary org-owner access, plus a client-controlled query param, on an unrelated spans-buffer change.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets passed into queryset slicing
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, uses the client-supplied cursor offset as the slice start (queryset[start_offset:stop]) and the comments say this is meant to reach rows beyond normal pagination bounds. Cursor.from_string already parses a negative offset with no check. Django querysets raise ValueError on negative slices, so this 500s; it does not implement reverse paging. BasePaginator was also changed so previous-page cursors keep a raw (possibly negative) offset on every endpoint that uses it. Negative offsets are not a safe or correct pagination mechanism here.

findings.title: Set keys switched to sorted sets with no migration
findings.body: add-buffer.lua and SpansBuffer now call ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZADD, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN on span-buf:s:* keys that existing consumers created with SADD/SUNIONSTORE. Redis returns WRONGTYPE if a key is still a set. During a rolling deploy, and for up to redis_ttl (default 3600s) after, insert and flush of in-flight segments fail, so spans are not buffered or cannot be flushed. There is no DEL/MIGRATE of old set keys and no WRONGTYPE handling.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and can double them
findings.body: zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MIN or MAX, so Redis's default SUM applies. When the same payload is already in both the destination segment key and the key being merged (retry, or span_key equal to set_key), the end_timestamp_precise score is added to itself. Eviction uses ZPOPMIN on those scores, so the wrong spans are dropped and ordering no longer matches end timestamps. The call should aggregate with MIN or MAX so a member keeps a single timestamp.

findings.title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The parent-redirect loop now stops at 1000 hops and the comment that this cap can fail to join deep segment trees was removed. On exit, the script still HSETs span_id to whatever set_span_id it stopped on and merges only that key. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are stored as split segments and later flushed with the wrong segment id, which the previous 10000 cap was explicitly there to avoid.

findings.title: Hardcoded eviction drops spans with no metric or config
findings.body: After merge, if the zset has more than 1000 members the script ZPOPMINs span_count-1000 members (lowest end_timestamp_precise) and returns success. The Python max_segment_spans limit (1001) and the flush-time segment_span_count_exceeded metric/error log were removed, and the cap is not passed into the script. The consumer will commit offsets for spans that were just deleted, with no signal that data was dropped, and the cap cannot be tuned via SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans. Eviction also runs on a span_count that stays 0-initialized unless a union happened, falling back to ZCARD only in that case; a union result that does not reflect members added only on the other key can under-count and leave the segment over the cap, or the next insert will delete the oldest payload including a root span while the has-root flag remains set.
